candidates.title: [Differential diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis pain: the role of subjective DAS28 scores, joint ultrasound, and digital biomarkers in therapeutic decision-making].
candidates.abstract: The purpose of this review is to examine the diagnostic challenges arising from the mathematical biases of the DAS28 index used in monitoring rheumatoid arthritis, as well as the psychological and neurobiological factors underlying patient-physician discordance. Furthermore, this paper aims to analyze the role of digital biomarkers in future decision-making. A structural characteristic of the DAS28 index is that its subjective components carry twice the weight of objective metrics. In cases of central sensitization, depression, or anxiety, this can result in "false-positive" disease activity, leading to unjustified and costly interventions, as well as ineffective therapy. Literature confirms that patient-physician discordance is one of the primary predictors of therapeutic failure, particularly in difficult-to-treat (D2T) cases. The application of the DAS28-P index can help identify pain-dominant phenotypes. Besides musculoskeletal ultrasound, new technologies, such as keystroke dynamics analysis or artificial intelligence-based imaging, offer objective measures to eliminate subjective biases. Modern rheumatological approaches should integrate psychological support, patient education, and pain modulation alongside immunosuppressive treatment. The implementation of digital biomarkers and hybrid care models not only improves the patient's quality of life but also generates significant system-level cost savings in healthcare. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(44): 1764-1771. A jelen összefoglaló célja a rheumatoid arthritis monitorozásában alkalmazott DAS28 index matematikai torzításaiból adódó diagnosztikus nehézségek, valamint a beteg-orvos diszkordancia hátterében álló pszichológiai és neurobiológiai tényezők áttekintése. A közlemény célja továbbá a digitális biomarkerek szerepének elemzése a jövőbeli döntéshozatalban. A DAS28 index szerkezeti sajátossága, hogy a szubjektív komponensek matematikai súlyozása a kétszerese az objektív mutatókénak. Ez centrális szenzitizáció, depresszió vagy szorongás esetén „álpozitív” aktivitást okozhat, ami indokolatlan és költséges beavatkozásokhoz és hatástalan terápiához vezethet. A szakirodalom igazolja, hogy a beteg-orvos diszkordancia a terápiás kudarc egyik legfőbb prediktora, különösen a nehezen kezelhető (D2T) esetekben. A DAS28-P index alkalmazása segíthet a fájdalomdomináns kórképek azonosításában. A mozgásszervi ultrahangvizsgálat mellett az új technológiák, mint a gépelési dinamika elemzése vagy a mesterséges intelligencián alapuló képalkotás, objektív mérőszámokat kínálnak a szubjektív torzítások kiküszöbölésére. A modern reumatológiai szemléletnek érdemes integrálnia a pszichológiai támogatást, a betegedukációt és a fájdalommodulációt az immunszuppresszív kezelés mellé. A digitális biomarkerek és a hibrid ellátási modellek alkalmazása nemcsak a beteg életminőségét javítja, hanem jelentős rendszerszintű költségmegtakarítást is eredményezhet az egészségügyben. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(44): 1764–1771.

candidates.title: Pilot study testing varenicline combined with a behavioral intervention for promoting smoking cessation and pain management among patients with cancer.
candidates.abstract: Many patients with cancer smoke and also experience pain. Smoking offers short-term pain relief but exacerbates pain long-term. We pilot tested the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of adding varenicline to a combined behavioral treatment that addresses smoking cessation and pain management. We conducted a single-arm pilot study in which we provided varenicline paired with a 4-session behavioral treatment that uses the same techniques to help people quit smoking and manage their pain. Our primary outcome was 7-day point prevalence abstinence at 6-months post-randomization. We recruited 19 patients with cancer. 80% of the patients who received the intervention rated it as "helpful" (4 or 5 out of 5) in helping them quit smoking; 60% rated it as helpful in managing their pain. Further, 94% would recommend the program to other patients with cancer. Roughly one-third (35%) (6/17) reported biochemically validated abstinence at 6 months post-randomization. We did not see improvements in reported pain but did see improvements in pain self-efficacy. Our pilot data suggest the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of this approach for promoting cessation. We need to refine aspects to help address pain, yet addressing pain in addition to smoking cessation might motivate more patients with cancer to join the program. The next step is to conduct a large randomized controlled trial to fully test the efficacy of the combined behavioral program with varenicline. A combined smoking cessation and pain program paired with varenicline might help patients with cancer quit smoking. NCT06029907.
candidates.journal: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice

candidates.title: Characterizing bone metastases and skeletal-related events in patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms utilizing 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography.
candidates.abstract: Tumors of neuroendocrine origin are a heterogenous group of related neoplasms which can arise from anywhere in the body. Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are categorized by site of origin, differentiation status and grade (Ki-67 expression and/or mitotic rate), with significant prognostic variability accordingly. Historically, the prevalence of bone metastasis is reported to be 6%-12% based on "first generation" (i.e., 111Indium pentetreotide [Octreoscan®]) somatostatin receptor imaging (SSRI). We conducted a retrospective cohort study including patients with well-differentiated NENs to determine the clinical and imaging characteristics of osseous metastases when evaluated with higher-sensitivity 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography (PET) scans, as well as determining fracture prevalence in selected sub-cohorts. We also developed a risk score analysis to assess risk of fracture in this cohort. Four hundred twenty-four patients were identified for inclusion. The median age was 61 years. Most patients were asymptomatic (64%), had sclerotic lesions (77%), Krenning 4 (71%), and had >3 sites (69%) of osseous disease. A high proportion of patients had osseous metastases at sites with high risk for fracture, including vertebra (82%), pelvis (63%), and peri-trochanteric femur (34%). Fifty-seven patients (13%) in the entire cohort suffered a fracture. Fracture prevalence was significantly lower in small bowel neuroendocrine tumors (NETs, 7%) and Grades 1 and 2 disease (8% and 9%, respectively), with higher prevalence in pancreatic NETs, paragangliomas/pheochromocytomas, lung carcinoid, and Grade 3 disease (≥20% for each; p-values <.05). Our study showed that the rate of osseous metastatic disease approximates 20% in well-differentiated NENs. Most bone metastases are asymptomatic and the risk of fracture is variable based on the primary site of disease and tumor grade. Our novel risk score analysis for fracture was designed to assist clinician decision making as to management of bone metastasis in this patient population.

candidates.title: Personalised acromegaly treatment: implementing precision medicine in the Gulf States.
candidates.abstract: Acromegaly management in the Gulf region is complicated by a high burden of metabolic comorbidity, frequent presentation with macroadenomas and suboptimal biochemical control in available regional cohorts. Conventional first-generation somatostatin receptor ligands achieve biochemical control in only 30-40% of patients, rates lower than those observed in European cohorts, necessitating precision medicine strategies. MRI signal and tumour granulation patterns represent the most widely available biomarkers in Gulf healthcare systems and enable precise treatment selection. These biomarkers may help predict poor first-generation therapy response while identifying patients who may benefit from pasireotide, an efficacious second-generation somatostatin receptor ligand with multi-receptor binding capacity. Implementation of biomarker-guided therapy in Gulf healthcare systems can optimize therapeutic outcomes while addressing regional challenges of delayed diagnosis and advanced disease presentation. Regional challenges specific to Gulf healthcare systems are identified and a practical biomarker-guided algorithm tailored for the GCC region is proposed to optimise treatment selection using readily available diagnostic tools. This approach is more appropriate for Gulf populations who present with more advanced disease characteristics that may benefit from precision-guided first-line treatment selection, representing a paradigm shift away from current guideline recommendations toward truly personalised medicine. This evolution from empirical to precision medicine represents a potential advancement for improving acromegaly management where complex metabolic phenotypes demand sophisticated treatment strategies.

candidates.title: Pulmonary edema during cesarean delivery secondary to Takotsubo syndrome revealing pheochromocytoma: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Acute pulmonary edema during delivery is a serious condition with a wide range of etiologies, including Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), a form of transient left ventricular dysfunction most often presenting as apical ballooning. We report the case of a 35-year-old woman who developed severe hypertension (205/130 mmHg), polypnea, and a drop in oxygen saturation to 80% during cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia. She received noninvasive ventilation while the cesarean section continued and was transferred to the intensive care unit. Point-of-care ultrasound showed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% with apical ballooning and diffuse B-lines on lung ultrasound. Computed tomography identified a right adrenal mass. A diagnosis of pulmonary edema complicating TTS was made, and the patient received furosemide and oxygen therapy. Further investigations, including urinary catecholamine metabolites, confirmed the diagnosis of pheochromocytoma. One week later, LVEF had recovered to 57% with mild residual apical hypokinesia and complete clinical recovery. The patient was then transferred to the surgical unit for management of the pheochromocytoma. This case demonstrates that TTS can cause pulmonary edema in the peripartum period, and that timely diagnosis is essential for a favorable outcome. Point-of-care ultrasound can be instrumental in guiding the assessment of such critical situations, and noninvasive ventilation may be of particular value in selected pregnant patients. This case also underscores the importance of an etiological workup and prompt treatment of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, especially when pheochromocytoma is suspected, since anesthesia and surgery can precipitate decompensation.

candidates.title: [Dynamic tongue reconstruction with reinnervated free gracilis muscle flap].
candidates.abstract: At our center, free flap reconstruction is the gold standard after subtotal or total glossectomy performed for oncological indications. In microvascular reconstructive surgery, several factors must be considered when selecting a flap. In the absence of a flap that meets all requirements perfectly, we strive to restore the functions that most significantly affect the quality of life. Removal of the tongue causes significant impairment of speech, swallowing, and taste sensation. A free flap containing a reinnervated muscle may be suitable for restoring partial tongue movements. Our report presents the use of a reinnervated gracilis musculocutaneous free flap following subtotal glossectomy. During free tissue transplantation, a tissue block removed from another part of the body is transplanted along with its supplying microvessels and nerves using microsurgical techniques. In addition to our standard postoperative management protocol, the flap healed uneventful, and oral feeding was fully restored on the 28th postoperative day. Images and swallowing X-ray taken 8 months postoperatively show the neotongue moving in a cranio-caudal direction. This is the first report of this method in the Hungarian literature. The dynamic movement and volume preservation of the transplanted muscle flap may prevent functional loss, thereby positively affecting the quality of life after treatment. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(44): 1785-1789. Az onkológiai indikációval végzett subtotalis vagy totalis nyelvresectiot követően kialakult szövethiányok pótlása centrumunkban szabad lebennyel történik. Kialakult szövethiányok pótlása centrumunkban szabad lebennyel történik. A microvascularis helyreállító sebészetben a lebeny kiválasztásakor több tényezőt kell figyelembe vennünk. Minden elvárásnak megfelelő lebeny hiányában az életminőséget leginkább érintő funkciók helyreállítására törekszünk. A nyelv eltávolítása során a beszéd, a nyelés és az ízérzés jelentősen károsodik. A nyelvmozgások egy részének helyreállítására alkalmas lehet a reinnervált izmot is tartalmazó szabad lebeny. Közleményünk subtotalis glossectomiát követő reinnervált gracilis musculocutaneus szabad lebeny alkalmazását mutatja be. A szabad szövet átültetése során a test más tájáról eltávolított szövetblokkot az azt ellátó mikroerekkel és ideggel együtt ültetjük át mikrosebészeti technika alkalmazásával. Standard posztoperatív kezelési protokollunk mellett a lebeny keringése mindvégig megtartott volt, a posztoperatív 28. napon a peroralis táplálást teljesen visszaállítottuk. A posztoperatív 8. hónapban készült képeken és nyelési röntgenfelvételen látható a craniocaudalisan mozgó neolingua. A hazai szakirodalomban először számolunk be erről a módszerről. Az átültetett izomlebeny dinamikus mozgása és volumentartása csökkentheti a funkcióvesztést, ezáltal pozitívan befolyásolhatja az onkológiai kezelés utáni életminőséget. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(44): 1785–1789.

candidates.title: [Reference guide for the clinical management of adult Langerhans cell histiocytosis (key points from the first edition, 2025)].
candidates.abstract: According to the registry of the Japanese Society of Hematology, adult histiocytic neoplasms are extremely rare, with approximately 40 cases reported annually, and the most common among them is Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH). Lesions may involve multiple organs, including bone, skin, lung, the central nervous system, and the endocrine system. Without a hematology perspective, the neoplastic nature of LCH may not be apparent, resulting in missed diagnoses. Central diabetes insipidus, anterior pituitary dysfunction, and LCH-associated neurodegeneration, once developed, often result in irreversible impairment. Because delayed therapeutic intervention can result in permanent organ damage, it is essential for hematologists to understand the "minimum initial management" required to protect patient outcomes. This review summarizes the key points of diagnosis and initial management in adult LCH based on the first edition of the Adult LCH Clinical Reference Guide (2025).
candidates.journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology

candidates.title: Newborn Screening for X-Linked Adrenoleukodystrophy: A Systematic Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD) is the most common leukodystrophy and peroxisomal disorder. It was added to newborn screening (NBS) programs following its first implementation in New York in 2013. Since then, X-ALD screening has expanded rapidly, although important differences exist among programs. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the global implementation of NBS for X-ALD, including screening methodologies, screening performance, prevalence estimates, genetic findings, and clinical follow-up outcomes. A systematic search of PubMed and EMBASE identified 13 publications describing NBS programs conducted between 2013 and June 2026. All programs used C26:0-lysophosphatidylcholine (C26:0-LPC) as the primary biomarker, although substantial heterogeneity was observed in analytical methodologies, cut-off values, screening algorithms, and follow-up strategies. Positive predictive values ranged from 9.1% to 100%, while screening detection rates varied from 1:3118 to 1:51,081, reflecting differences in study design, screening population, sample size, and screening approaches. Variants of uncertain significance (VUS) accounted for 52.6% of individuals detected with classified ABCD1 variant findings, representing a major challenge for genetic counseling and clinical management. Most identified newborns were asymptomatic at diagnosis, supporting the role of NBS in enabling early surveillance for adrenal insufficiency and cerebral disease before irreversible manifestations occur. In addition, differences between universal and sex-specific screening strategies highlight ongoing clinical and ethical debates regarding the scope of X-ALD NBS. Overall, current evidence supports the feasibility of NBS for X-ALD and its ability to enable presymptomatic ascertainment and early clinical surveillance; however, greater harmonization of screening protocols, improved variant interpretation, and long-term outcome studies are needed to optimize program performance and clinical benefit.

candidates.title: Targeting RIPK1-NF-κB crosstalk: A novel perspective on necroptosis in Alzheimer's Disease.
candidates.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative condition characterised by gradual neuronal degradation, resulting in cognitive decline and memory loss. Multiple pathogenic mechanisms drive the progression of the disease, including amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau accumulation (neurofibrillary tangles), mitochondrial dysfunction, synaptic loss, chronic neuroinflammation, and neuro​nal death. Neuronal loss in AD occurs through various forms of regulated cell death, including apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, parthanatos, and necroptosis, each characterised by specific pathways and subsequent inflammatory consequences. Despite decades of focus on apoptosis and necrosis as the primary modes of neuronal loss, necroptosis has remained relatively understudied until recently. Necroptosis is a caspase-independent, inflammatory cell death pathway governed by the RIPK1-RIPK3-MLKL signalling axis. Activation of this pathway disrupts plasma membrane integrity, triggering the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) that sustain a self-propagating cycle of neuroinflammation and secondary neuronal loss. Crucially, RIPK1 signalling is closely linked to nuclear factor-[Formula: see text]B (NF-[Formula: see text]B), a principal modulator of inflammatory and cell-survival mechanisms. Although NF-[Formula: see text]B activation can facilitate neuronal survival under physiological conditions, its sustained activation in the AD brain promotes the synthesis of pro-inflammatory mediators, thereby accelerating neurodegeneration. This review discusses the emerging role of RIPK1-mediated necroptosis in AD and examines its functional interaction with NF-[Formula: see text]B signalling in driving neuroinflammation. Additionally, it examines emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the RIPK1-NF-[Formula: see text]B axis to alter disease progression and achieve disease-modifying potential in AD.

candidates.title: Pregnancy in Autoimmune Polyglandular Syndrome Type 3c With Graves' Disease and Myasthenia Gravis: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 3c (APS3c), characterized by autoimmune thyroid disease with another organ-specific autoimmune disorder in the absence of adrenal insufficiency, is an uncommon presentation. Its coexistence with Graves' disease and myasthenia gravis (MG) is rare and poses additional diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly when complicated by thyroid storm and pregnancy. We report the ongoing management of a 22-year-old woman with this combination of autoimmune disorders. She was admitted with thyroid storm diagnosed using the Burch-Wartofsky Point Scale and Japan Thyroid Association criteria after a 15-month history of weight loss, heat intolerance, diaphoresis, anxiety, palpitations, unilateral ptosis, and fatigable proximal upper-extremity weakness. Graves' disease and MG were diagnosed based on clinical findings, positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin and acetylcholine receptor antibodies, and electrophysiological evidence of a postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder. In the absence of clinical or biochemical evidence of primary adrenal insufficiency, the coexistence of autoimmune thyroid disease and MG supported a diagnosis of APS3c on the Neufeld and Blizzard classification. Despite methimazole (15 mg/day) and pyridostigmine (600 mg/day) therapy, and good adherence to treatment, biochemical hyperthyroidism persisted and progressed to thyroid storm. During outpatient follow-up, an intrauterine pregnancy was confirmed. Methimazole was withheld during the first trimester while the patient remained clinically stable despite persistent biochemical hyperthyroidism, and it was resumed thereafter. At the time of writing, the pregnancy remains ongoing under multidisciplinary care involving endocrinology, neurology, internal medicine, and maternal-fetal medicine, with serial maternal monitoring, planned third-trimester antibody reassessment, targeted fetal ultrasonography, perinatal planning, and neonatal surveillance. This case highlights APS3c as an important diagnostic framework for the coexistence of Graves' disease and MG and illustrates how management must be continually reassessed in the setting of thyroid storm and pregnancy. Maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes remain pending.

candidates.title: Pituitary Apoplexy Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism in a Neurologically Complex Patient: A Diagnostic Challenge.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary apoplexy is a rare endocrine emergency resulting from either acute haemorrhage or infarction within the pituitary gland. Although apoplexy occurs most frequently in a pre-existing pituitary adenoma, apoplexy could be the first presentation of a previously unknown adenoma. Acute headaches, visual disturbances, and neurological symptoms are common presenting symptoms in apoplexy; however, these symptoms may overlap with other neurological emergencies, which necessitate a holistic approach of clinical, radiological, and hormonal evaluation for suspected cases of apoplexy to confirm the diagnosis. Here we present a diagnostically challenging case of a 66-year-old man who presented with a sudden severe headache. His background history included a presumed intraventricular neurocytoma under surveillance. Initial CT head scan suggested possible haemorrhage within a known intraventricular mass (neurocytoma) with no obvious changes within the pituitary gland. However, subsequent MRI head demonstrated radiological features consistent with pituitary apoplexy. Later in his admission, he exhibited bilateral peripheral visual field constriction and early papilledema on fundoscopy. Hormonal testing showed evidence of hypopituitarism. The patient was managed conservatively with intravenous hydrocortisone replacement. During admission, he developed bilateral pulmonary emboli, for which he was treated with anticoagulation. While he was on anticoagulation, he developed intracranial haemorrhage, which led to his death after discharge from the hospital. This case demonstrates the importance of considering pituitary apoplexy in a challenging radiological and clinical presentation. A pre-existing neurological lesion (neurocytoma) makes a holistic approach, including MRI imaging and early hormonal evaluation are essential for timely diagnosis and treatment of pituitary apoplexy. The clinical challenge of having concurrent haemorrhagic and thrombotic events necessitates an individualised approach after balancing the benefits and risks of using anticoagulation treatment.

candidates.title: Scleroderma-Like Phenotype in a Patient With Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis and Acromegaly: A Triple Diagnostic Challenge.
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis, transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, and acromegaly are rare disorders that share several clinical manifestations, including skin thickening, heart failure, dysphagia, fatigue, and soft tissue enlargement. Their coexistence is exceptionally rare and poses a significant diagnostic challenge, increasing the risk of premature diagnostic closure. We report a 78-year-old man who developed progressive diffuse skin thickening following spinal cord stimulator revision. Positive RNA polymerase III antibodies supported a diagnosis of diffuse systemic sclerosis. Evaluation of worsening edema and exertional dyspnea revealed severe concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with relative apical sparing on echocardiography, and technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy confirmed transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Persistent macroglossia, coarse facial features, prior carpal tunnel syndrome, and a remote history of increasing ring and shoe size prompted endocrine evaluation, which demonstrated elevated insulin-like growth factor-1 levels, failure of growth hormone suppression, and a pituitary macroadenoma consistent with acromegaly. The patient underwent successful transsphenoidal resection with biochemical remission. This case highlights the importance of reconsidering the differential diagnosis when clinical features are not fully explained by an established diagnosis. Recognizing atypical and discordant findings prevented premature diagnostic closure and led to the identification of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and acromegaly in a patient with a rapidly progressive scleroderma-like phenotype.

candidates.title: Transfemoral transcaval adrenal biopsy: a technical report and review of adrenal biopsy approaches.
candidates.abstract: Despite advances in cross-sectional imaging, adrenal biopsy plays a role in a small subset of lesions that remain indeterminate after complete imaging work-up or in which tissue diagnosis would alter management. Anatomic constraints around the adrenal glands can make safe percutaneous access technically challenging. This technical report describes a transfemoral transcaval approach to biopsy of a right adrenal mass directly abutting the inferior vena cava (IVC) that was not safely accessible by conventional percutaneous routes. Additionally, a concise review of contemporary adrenal biopsy indications and access routes is performed. Adapted from transfemoral transcaval liver biopsy, the technique uses right common femoral venous access, positioning of a reshaped metal guide cannula within the IVC at the level of the lesion adjacent to the right renal vein, and deployment of a core biopsy needle across the caval wall under combined fluoroscopic and ultrasound guidance, with cone-beam CT confirmation of needle position and completion venography to exclude caval injury. Diagnostic tissue was obtained without periprocedural complication; histopathology demonstrated an unexpected pheochromocytoma, a finding discussed here in detail due to its implications for pre-procedure biochemical evaluation. This limited experience demonstrates technical feasibility in carefully selected patients. The safety and comparative effectiveness of the technique require evaluation in larger series.

candidates.title: Beyond Digoxin Toxicity: A Fatal Case of BRASH Syndrome Triggered by Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
candidates.abstract: Bradycardia, renal failure, atrioventricular (AV) nodal blockade, shock, and hyperkalemia (BRASH) syndrome is a rare, life-threatening clinical condition caused by the synergistic interaction between hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction, and AV nodal blocking agents, resulting in severe bradycardia and hemodynamic instability. Early recognition is often challenging due to its nonspecific presentation. We report the case of an 82-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, ischemic heart disease, congestive cardiac failure, chronic kidney disease, and chronic digoxin therapy who presented with abdominal pain, confusion, dizziness, hypotension, and profound bradycardia. Investigations demonstrated severe hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury on top of chronic kidney disease, hyponatremia, and electrocardiographic changes consistent with hyperkalemia. Initial differential diagnoses included mesenteric ischemia, adrenal insufficiency, and digoxin toxicity; however, imaging excluded bowel ischemia, cortisol levels were normal, and serum digoxin at the therapeutic level. Community-acquired pneumonia complicated by sepsis was identified as the precipitating trigger for BRASH syndrome. Despite intensive treatment, including hyperkalemia management, isoprenaline infusion, antibiotics, corticosteroids, and supportive care, the patient's condition progressively deteriorated, culminating in multiorgan failure and death shortly afterward. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of BRASH syndrome and emphasizes the importance of early recognition and targeted management to interrupt the vicious cycle and improve clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Osteoporosis, sarcopenia, locomotive syndrome, and frailty in age-related spinal kyphosis.
candidates.abstract: Age-related kyphosis is a common manifestation of musculoskeletal aging associated with falls, mobility decline, reduced participation, and respiratory compromise in severe cases. This narrative review summarizes its relationships with osteoporosis, sarcopenia, locomotive syndrome, and frailty. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for English-language publications from database inception through December 31, 2025. Relevant evidence was reviewed narratively. Observational studies indicate that osteoporosis-associated vertebral fragility is an important structural contributor to kyphotic progression through clinically apparent or unrecognized vertebral fractures and progressive vertebral deformity. Degenerative disc changes and local trunk muscle dysfunction may also contribute through altered spinal loading and reduced active postural support. Evidence linking generalized sarcopenia to kyphosis remains inconsistent, whereas local trunk muscle dysfunction and poor paraspinal muscle quality may be more directly relevant. Kyphosis may coexist with locomotive syndrome and physical frailty, but these associations do not establish causality. Assessment should include bone mineral density, vertebral fracture status, regional and global sagittal alignment, trunk muscle function, and mobility. Management should combine appropriate osteoporosis treatment, trunk-focused exercise, posture training, and nutritional support. Further longitudinal and interventional studies are needed to clarify causal relationships and determine whether treatment preserves mobility and independence.
candidates.journal: Journal of bone and mineral metabolism

candidates.title: Management of congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency: an update.
candidates.abstract: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) represents a group of autosomal recessive disorders characterized by enzyme deficiencies thatimpair adrenal steroidogenesis, most commonly due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. The biochemical defects in CAH translate to a spectrumof clinical consequences, which include adrenal insufficiency, genital ambiguity or disordered sex development, infertility, short stature,and an increased risk of metabolic syndrome during adolescence and adulthood. The severity and clinical features of CAH vary dependingon the enzymatic defect, residual enzymatic activity, the age of presentation, and genotype. This review comprehensively covers the genetic background, classification, and clinical spectrum of CAH, including classical and non-classical forms. We discuss the importance and implementation of neonatal screening programs for early diagnosis and intervention. Specialattention is given to differences in treatment approaches between children and adolescents, highlighting the challenges of optimizingglucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid therapy across developmental stages. Furthermore, we present emerging novel pharmacologicalagents currently in clinical trials aimed at improving disease management. The review also addresses potential complications associatedwith CAH, such as metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular risks, and bone health issues. Emphasizing a patient-centered approach, wehighlight the critical role of experienced endocrinologists in delivering individualized care to improve long-term outcomes. Our review summarizes the current knowledge, aims to guide clinicians in evidence-based management and highlights ongoing research into innovativetherapies for CAH.

candidates.title: [Testicular teratoma with somatic-type malignancy].
candidates.abstract: Most adult testicular tumors are germ cell tumors, among which teratoma may exhibit somatic-type malignant transformation. This phenomenon is uncommon (reported in approximately 3-8% of cases), may show carcinomatous or sarcomatous differentiation and is associated with an unfavorable prognosis and resistance to conventional therapies. We present the case of a 51-year-old man with metastatic testicular cancer. The tumor removed by semicastration was histologically identified as a rhabdomyosarcoma arising in a postpubertal teratoma. Due to the metastatic disease, cytotoxic treatment was initiated with VIP (etoposide-ifosfamide-cisplatin) regimen, followed by an EP (etoposide-cisplatin) protocol because of ifosfamide intolerance. Somatic-type malignant transformation of testicular teratoma is a rare entity that poses significant therapeutic challenges. The presence of a rhabdomyosarcoma component is associated with poor prognosis and often necessitates a sarcoma-oriented oncologic approach. Standard germ cell tumor chemotherapy protocols are generally of limited efficacy; therefore, a multidisciplinary approach, accurate histopathological diagnosis, and appropriate selection of therapy are essential. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(44): 1790-1795. A felnőttkori heredaganatok többsége csírasejtes tumor, amelyek között a teratoma szomatikus típusú malignus transzformációt mutathat. Ez a jelenség ritka (kb. 3–8%), szövetileg társulhat carcinomás vagy sarcomás differenciálódással, amelyhez kedvezőtlen kimenetel és a konvencionális terápiával szembeni rezisztencia társulhat. Egy 51 éves férfi beteg áttétes heretumor miatt került kivizsgálásra. A semicastratio révén eltávolított daganat szövettanilag postpubertalis típusú teratoma talaján kialakult rhabdomyosarcomának bizonyult. Az áttétes betegség miatt előbb VIP- (etopozid-ifoszfamid-ciszplatin), majd az ifoszfamidintolerancia miatt EP- (etopozid-ciszplatin) protokoll szerinti kezelés indult. A teratoma szomatikus malignus transzformációja szokatlan jelenség, amelynek kezelése kihívást jelent. A rhabdomyosarcoma komponens jelenléte rossz prognózissal jár, és gyakran sarcomaorientált onkológiai megközelítést tesz indokolttá. A standard kemoterápiás protokollok általában limitált hatékonyságúak, ezért a multidiszciplináris megközelítés, az adekvát szövettani diagnózis és a megfelelő terápiás protokoll kiválasztása kulcsfontosságú. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(44): 1790–1795.

candidates.title: Association between pathological subtypes of PitNETs and postoperative biochemical remission in acromegaly.
candidates.abstract: To assess whether transcription factor (TF)- and hormone-defined pathological subtypes of pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are associated with postoperative biochemical remission in acromegaly. Consecutive acromegaly patients who underwent surgery between January 2015 and October 2025 with a minimum 3-month follow-up were enrolled. Patients were classified by TF and hormone expression patterns: pure vs. non-pure PIT-1 positive, and pure vs. non-pure GH positive. Drawing on target trial emulation-derived design principles, propensity score overlap weighting (OW) balanced six prespecified confounders and covariate balance was confirmed after weighting. Associations between pathological subtypes and postoperative biochemical remission were examined using weighted Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses. Overall, 93.4% had macroadenomas; the overall remission rate was 51.0%. Pure PIT-1 positive and pure GH positive tumors represented 62.3% and 19.2%, respectively. After OW, for both TF and hormone classification, no statistically significant difference in postoperative cumulative biochemical remission was observed between the pure and non-pure groups (TF: P = 0.824; hormone: P = 0.444). Weighted Cox regression analyses confirmed that neitherthe TF-based (HR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.53-1.42, P = 0.578) nor the hormone-based (HR = 1.52, 95% CI: 0.62-3.75, P = 0.362) classification of PitNETs predicted postoperative biochemical remission. Higher preoperative IGF-1 index was a significant negative predictor only in the TF-based group (HR = 0.51, 95%CI 0.37-0.74, P < 0.001). Pathological subtypes of PitNETs do not independently predict surgical remission in acromegaly. The preoperative IGF-1 index showed limited, context-dependent prognostic value. Future multimodal models integrating histology, imaging, and genomics may improve prognostic accuracy.

candidates.title: VIP-Mediated Syndromes: Contrasting Presentations and Multidisciplinary Management of Two Rare Neuroendocrine Tumors.
candidates.abstract: Vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)-secreting tumors are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms that cause severe secretory diarrhea and electrolyte abnormalities. We describe 2 atypical cases requiring multidisciplinary care. One patient had a VIP-secreting pheochromocytoma with elevated VIP and metanephrine levels; symptoms improved after adrenalectomy. The second had a metastatic small intestinal neuroendocrine tumor with persistent VIP-mediated diarrhea despite debulking and somatostatin analog therapy, complicated by anal fissures, trans-sphincteric perianal fistula, and neuropathic pelvic pain. These cases highlight morbidity and potential complications associated with extrapancreatic VIP hypersecretion and the value of coordinated multidisciplinary management to improve outcomes and quality of life.

candidates.title: The Steroid Symptom Questionnaire Multiple Myeloma (SSQ-MM): translation and cross-cultural adaptation into Danish and Norwegian and initial psychometric evaluation of the Norwegian version.
candidates.abstract: The Steroid Symptom Questionnaire - Multiple Myeloma (SSQ-MM) was developed to assess patient-reported side effects of corticosteroid treatment in multiple myeloma (MM) patients. This study aimed to translate and culturally adapt the SSQ-MM into Danish and Norwegian, and to provide an initial evaluation of the psychometric properties of the Norwegian version. Translation and cultural adaptation followed ISPOR good practice guidelines, including forward-backward translation and cognitive debriefing interviews with patients and clinicians. Psychometric evaluation was conducted in newly diagnosed Norwegian MM patients receiving weekly dexamethasone. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha. Construct validity was explored through correlations with EORTC QLQ-C30 constructs and known-groups comparisons based on ECOG performance status. Responsiveness was evaluated across three time points. The Danish and Norwegian translations were considered relevant and acceptable by patients and clinicians. The Norwegian version demonstrated acceptable internal consistency for the total score (α = 0.74) and psychological subscale (α = 0.81). Correlation patterns were generally consistent with predefined hypotheses and known-groups validity was supported by differences in symptom scores according to ECOG performance status. Responsiveness analyses demonstrated significant increases in the total score and several steroid-related symptoms during treatment, whereas fewer changes were observed following treatment discontinuation. Overall, symptom levels were lower than those reported in the original Australian validation study. Findings from the Norwegian cohort provide preliminary evidence supporting the reliability, construct validity, known-groups validity, and responsiveness of the Norwegian SSQ-MM. Further studies in larger, diverse MM populations are needed to further evaluate its measurement properties.
candidates.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation

candidates.title: Adrenal Incidentalomas: Do All Patients Require a Biochemical Workup?
candidates.abstract: Adrenal incidentalomas are common findings on cross-sectional imaging, and most represent benign adrenocortical adenomas. The traditional approach has been to perform biochemical testing in essentially every patient to exclude pheochromocytoma, cortisol excess, and, when clinical suspicion is present, primary aldosteronism. However, this algorithmic approach may result in overinvestigation in light of improved adrenal imaging, recognition of the low prevalence of clinically important hormone excess, and concerns about false-positive testing. The 2023 European Society of Endocrinology guideline continues to recommend clinical and endocrine assessment for all patients but provides an important imaging-based nuance: in a homogeneous adrenal mass with ≤10 Hounsfield units on unenhanced computed tomography, the probability of pheochromocytoma is extremely low, and biochemical testing for metanephrines may reasonably be omitted. In contrast, testing for mild autonomous cortisol secretion remains broadly recommended because clinically silent cortisol excess is associated with metabolic syndrome and potential morbidity. This review examines the arguments for and against universal biochemical workup and proposes a risk-stratified approach for clinicians.

candidates.title: Retinal Microvascular and Peripapillary Profiles in Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion Versus Nonfunctioning Adrenal Adenomas.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is associated with increased cardiometabolic morbidity, but its relationship with the retinal microcirculation is unknown. We compared retinal and peripapillary microvascular parameters between MACS and nonfunctioning adrenal adenoma (NFA) and, secondarily, examined their associations with continuously modeled post-dexamethasone cortisol. Methods: In this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study, 98 patients (45 NFA, 53 MACS) were included, and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and structural OCT data from one eye per patient were analyzed. The primary outcome was whole-image deep capillary plexus (DCP) vessel density. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and cardiometabolic comorbidities; secondary analyses were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (q values). Results: OCTA was evaluable in 89 patients. The primary outcome did not differ significantly between groups in the main analysis (NFA vs. MACS, 48.64 ± 5.71% vs. 47.31 ± 5.77%; adjusted difference -1.29 percentage points, 95% CI -3.97 to 1.38; p = 0.339) or in any sensitivity analysis. In secondary analyses, superior retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness was greater in MACS (β = 17.38 µm; q < 0.001) and increased with ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) (β = 13.74 µm; q = 0.010). Higher ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) was also associated with lower parafoveal DCP (β = -2.72 percentage points; p = 0.013) and inside-disc radial peripapillary capillary vessel density (β = -3.13 percentage points; p = 0.026), which did not survive multiplicity correction; no superficial capillary plexus sector was associated with either exposure (all p ≥ 0.37). Conclusions: MACS was not significantly associated with whole-image DCP vessel density. The secondary associations with continuous cortisol are cross-sectional and hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

candidates.title: Probable Hypophysitis Recognized More Than Two Years After Pembrolizumab Discontinuation.
candidates.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated hypophysitis is an uncommon but clinically important endocrine immune-related adverse event. We report a 70-year-old man with a history of non-small cell lung cancer previously treated with approximately two years of pembrolizumab, with his last dose administered approximately 28 months before presentation. He developed progressive fatigue, anorexia, hypotension, functional decline, and confusion and was subsequently hospitalized with multifocal pneumonia and septic shock. Although the infection and hemodynamic instability improved, encephalopathy, weakness, poor oral intake, and dysphagia persisted. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated new pituitary enlargement compared with imaging obtained approximately three months earlier. Dedicated pituitary imaging showed enlargement measuring approximately 1.5 × 2.0 cm without definite differential enhancement to suggest a pituitary adenoma. Endocrine testing demonstrated a cortisol level of 3.3 µg/dL with an inappropriately low adrenocorticotropic hormone level of 6.5 pg/mL, free thyroxine of 0.36 ng/dL with thyroid-stimulating hormone of 2.0 µIU/mL, suppressed gonadotropins, and testosterone <10 ng/dL, supporting central adrenal insufficiency and central hypothyroidism with marked gonadal-axis suppression. Cerebrospinal fluid cytology and paraneoplastic studies were unrevealing. The patient was treated with hydrocortisone before thyroid hormone replacement and subsequently showed progressive improvement in mental status, oral intake, and participation in rehabilitation. This case highlights that pituitary immune-related adverse events may be recognized long after pembrolizumab discontinuation and emphasizes the importance of considering prior immune checkpoint inhibitor exposure in patients with unexplained endocrine and constitutional decline.

candidates.title: Acute Sheehan Syndrome Presenting as Panhypopituitarism and Reversible Cardiac Dysfunction in a Patient With Sickle Cell Disease: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sheehan syndrome is an uncommon cause of hypopituitarism resulting from ischemic pituitary necrosis following severe postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) and hypotension. Its presentation can be delayed and non-specific, and it is rarely reported in the context of mild PPH with severe hemolysis. Here, we describe a 31-year-old woman with underlying sickle cell disease (SCD) who developed panhypopituitarism and reversible cardiac dysfunction after an 11-week period of progressive symptoms following spontaneous vaginal delivery complicated by an estimated blood loss of 700 mL and severe hemolysis. Pituitary hormonal replacement therapy, together with heart failure treatment, resulted in marked clinical and biochemical improvement, with normalization of metabolic abnormalities and recovery of cardiac function. This case suggests a possible association between Sheehan syndrome and postpartum blood loss of 700 mL accompanied by severe hemolysis, though this remains hypothetical based on a single case.

candidates.title: Addison's Disease Mimicking Cerebral Salt Wasting Syndrome: A Case of Severe Hyponatremia.
candidates.abstract: Hyponatremia is a common electrolyte abnormality with varying degrees of severity. It can be asymptomatic if mild and can cause convulsions and coma if severe. Systematic investigation of hyponatremia helps to find out the etiology and proper management. Here, we are presenting the case of a 67-year-old man who presented with vomiting, hyperpigmentation, and hypovolemic hyponatremia due to Addison's disease. Evaluation of hyponatremia showed elevated urinary sodium as expected in Addison's disease, but there was hypouricemia with increased fractional excretion of uric acid suggestive of cerebral salt wasting syndrome. Even with the correct diagnosis, wrong medication interval can cause inadequate rise in serum sodium. Mild thyroid-stimulating hormone elevation can occur in untreated isolated Addison's disease. Addison's disease should always be considered in unexplained hyponatremia even if laboratory findings are suggestive of cerebral salt wasting syndrome. Hyponatremia in Addison's disease may respond poorly to hypertonic saline until glucocorticoid deficiency is corrected, and steroid and fluid replacement is essential and lifesaving.

candidates.title: Circ_0018814 promotes the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells in ankylosing spondylitis by regulating the miR-944/KLF4 axis.
candidates.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease primarily affecting the spine and sacroiliac joints. This study investigated the impact of circ_0018814 on the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in AS through the regulation of the miR-944/KLF4 axis and to evaluate its potential role in the progression of AS. GSE203155 was used as an exploratory screening dataset to identify candidate circRNAs associated with osteogenic differentiation in AS-MSCs. Circ_0018814 expression was further evaluated in bone marrow samples and primary MSCs. The effects of circ_0018814 on osteogenic differentiation markers (ALP, RUNX2, COL1A1) in MSCs from AS patients were assessed using western blot, ALP assay, and alizarin red S staining. The targeting relationship between circ_0018814, KLF4, and miR-944 was confirmed through luciferase reporter and RNA immunoprecipitation assays. Fluorescence in situ hybridization was used for cellular localization. Further experiments in a murine AS model evaluated the impact of circ_0018814 on AS lesions and MSC differentiation. The results showed that overexpression of circ_0018814 significantly enhanced the expression of osteogenic markers ALP, RUNX2, and COL1A1, and promoted the osteogenic differentiation of MSCs. Additionally, circ_0018814 regulated KLF4 expression by targeting miR-944. Inhibition of miR-944 upregulated KLF4 expression and promoted osteogenic differentiation. In the AS mouse model, downregulation of circ_0018814 significantly alleviated spinal lesions, restored normal expression levels of miR-944 and KLF4, and reduced disease-related osteogenic changes. This study demonstrates that circ_0018814 plays an important role in the pathological progression of AS by regulating the miR-944/KLF4 axis. circ_0018814 may serve as a novel potential therapeutic target for AS, providing new insights for future treatment strategies. However, the in vivo findings should be interpreted cautiously because tail vein delivery of lentiviral constructs is not MSC-specific.

candidates.title: Newly Diagnosed Graves' Disease Followed by the Discovery of a Cavernous Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysm Causing Panhypopituitarism: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sellar and parasellar vascular lesions are rare causes of pituitary dysfunction and may mimic pituitary adenomas or other sellar masses. Cavernous internal carotid artery (ICA) aneurysms can cause hypopituitarism through compression of the pituitary gland or stalk, but diagnosis may be delayed when symptoms are initially attributed to a more common endocrine disorder. We report a 37-year-old man who presented with six weeks of unintentional weight loss, fatigue, heat intolerance, excessive sweating, anxiety, tremor, and tachycardia. Initial evaluation showed suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), elevated total triiodothyronine (T3), positive thyrotropin receptor antibody, positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin, and a hypervascular thyroid gland on ultrasound, consistent with Graves' disease. He was started on methimazole and atenolol. Although thyroid function tests improved, he developed persistent neck discomfort, prompting contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), which revealed an enhancing sellar mass. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a T2-hypointense sellar lesion with internal flow artifact, and CT angiography confirmed a saccular aneurysm of the cavernous segment of the right ICA. Pituitary hormone evaluation demonstrated secondary adrenal insufficiency, central hypothyroidism, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, growth hormone (GH) deficiency, and mild hyperprolactinemia, consistent with panhypopituitarism from pituitary compression. The patient was started on prednisone and levothyroxine, and atenolol and prednisone were subsequently discontinued before endovascular embolization was performed. At follow-up, symptoms improved, but panhypopituitarism persisted. This case highlights the importance of reassessing patients when endocrine symptoms evolve despite an initially appropriate diagnosis.

candidates.title: Proteomic profiling of somatotropinoma subtypes reveals TNIP1 overexpression in sparsely granulated tumors in a small discovery cohort.
candidates.abstract: The molecular mechanisms underlying the clinical differences between densely granulated (DG) and sparsely granulated (SG) somatotroph tumors remain poorly understood. To identify significant molecular differences between these subtypes, we performed quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomic profiling followed by validation of the differentially-identified proteins. Label-free quantitative proteomic analysis was performed on SG somatotroph adenomas (SGSAs, n = 3) and DG somatotroph adenomas (DGSAs, n = 3), with each sample analyzed in technical triplicate. Key findings were subsequently validated using immunohistochemistry (IHC, n = 64), immunofluorescence (IF, n = 24), and Western blotting (WB, n = 18). Proteomic profiling identified TNFAIP3-interacting protein 1 (TNIP1) as the most significantly over-expressed protein, and coenzyme Q6 monooxygenase (COQ6) as the most significantly under-expressed protein, in SGSAs compared with DGSAs. Higher TNIP1 expression in SGSAs was significantly associated with IGF-1 [%ULN], larger tumor diameter, greater tumor volume, higher Knosp grade and SSTR5 expression. In contrast, COQ6 expression showed significant negative correlations with tumor diameter, tumor volume, Knosp grade, and SSTR5 expression. These findings indicate strong associations between TNIP1 and COQ6 expression and tumor characteristics, along with differences in cell adhesion and signaling pathways. SGSAs and DGSAs exhibit distinct proteomic profiles. Increased TNIP1 and reduced COQ6 expression, together with alterations in cell adhesion and signaling pathways in SGSA, may contribute to the molecular and phenotypic differences underlying these somatotroph tumor subtypes.

candidates.title: Utility of the ACTH/cortisol ratio for differentiating pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism.
candidates.abstract: No simple, blood-based biomarker to estimate tumor size in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism (PDH) has been evaluated. Determine whether the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)/cortisol ratio differentiates pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with PDH and correlates with pituitary size. Seventy privately-owned dogs with PDH (microadenomas, n = 30; macroadenomas, n = 40). Retrospective multicenter observational study. Endogenous ACTH and cortisol concentrations obtained at the same time point before treatment were used to calculate the ACTH/cortisol ratio. Pituitary tumor size was classified using the pituitary-to-brain (P/B) ratio. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and multivariable logistic regression. Dogs with macroadenomas had significantly higher ACTH/cortisol ratios than dogs with microadenomas (median, 9.12; IQR, 6.46-14.28 vs median, 4.90; IQR, 3.08-8.10; P < .001). The ratio showed moderate discrimination for differentiating macroadenomas from microadenomas with an area under the curve of 0.77 (95% CI, 0.66-0.89; P < .001). A cutoff >5.69 yielded 85% sensitivity and 60% specificity (positive likelihood ratio 2.13), whereas a higher ratio >11.74 achieved 90% specificity and 35% sensitivity (positive likelihood ratio 3.50). The ACTH/cortisol ratio showed moderate positive correlation with pituitary size (Spearman's ρ = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.26-0.64; P < .001) and remained independently associated with macroadenoma classification in multivariable analysis (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.05-1.40). The ACTH/cortisol ratio is associated with pituitary tumor size in dogs with PDH and may support clinical risk stratification, particularly when advanced imaging is unavailable.
